api.description: Destination for the anchor. GPUI has no in-app navigation graph, so `href` opens through the OS handler (`App::open_url`) on press.
Where to open the linked document. The port has no browser navigation or HTTP transport — `href` opens through the OS handler — so there is nothing for a target to control.
Relationship between the documents. Meaningless without an anchor element handed to a browser; the OS handler receives only the URL string.
Prompts a file download. The OS handler decides what to do with the URL; the port has no HTTP transport to fetch and save it.
Disables pointer and keyboard interaction: the disabled opacity, no pointer reach, and no tab stop.
Custom classes merged with the default styles.
Content rendered inside the link. The port composes it as the label text plus an optional icon element, ordered by where the icon belongs (v3 orders `Link.Icon` among the children).
Fired when the link is activated, in addition to opening `href`. The callback receives GPUI's ClickEvent rather than React Aria's PressEvent.
Whether the element should receive focus on render. A link is not otherwise a focus target here, so this also makes it one; a disabled link is skipped by Tab and must not grab focus either.

Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function. GPUI has no DOM props to spread onto a caller-built element, so the closure receives the interactive half alone (`isHovered`, `isPressed`, `isFocused`, `isFocusVisible`, `isDisabled`) and draws the content; the root keeps the `href`, `onPress`, focus and disabled wiring either way.

Custom icon content. A childless `Link.Icon` renders v3's built-in arrow with `data-default-icon="true"` and its `ms-1 pb-1.5` spacing, and that default arrow has no port path: `icon(element)` is the custom-children path only, so the port draws no icon at all without it. `icon_first(true)` moves the icon before the label the way v3's child ordering does.
Additional CSS classes.

parts.name: Link

parts.name: Link.Icon
parts.description: `pointer-events-none inline-flex size-[0.75em] shrink-0 items-center justify-center text-current opacity-60`, raised to full opacity on hover, press and focus. `[data-default-icon=true]` adds `ms-1 pb-1.5`, but that rule belongs only to the childless built-in arrow, which the port does not draw; `icon(element)` is the arbitrary-children path and gets no default-icon spacing. The port draws the caller's element verbatim, flush against the label, without the em-sized box or the default 60% opacity.

Takes the underline decoration to full `decoration-muted`.

api.description: Avatar size: 32/40/48px edge, with `sm` rounding one step tighter and `lg` stepping the fallback text up to 16px.
Fallback color theme. The base avatar fills `bg-default` for every color — the color recolours the initials via the soft-foreground token.
Visual style variant. `soft` clears the base fill and paints `bg-{role}-soft` with the same soft foreground.
Additional CSS classes.

Image source URL. A plain string or path loads through gpui's asset system (a parseable URI is fetched, anything else is an embedded resource); the gpui `ImageSource::Image` / `Render` / `Custom` variants are the explicit parts for images the app already holds or loads itself.
Callback when the image loads successfully and replaces the fallback. Fires once per source, on the first observed success, outside the layout phase; there is no event payload to hand over.
Callback when there's an error loading the image; the fallback initials replace the image on that same failure. Fires once per source; no event payload.
The image `srcset` attribute for responsive images. Browser-only: gpui's asset system resolves one resource per source and never selects between candidates.
The image `sizes` attribute. Browser-only hint for `srcset` selection; there is no viewport-density image pick to hint.
Alternative text for the image. GPUI 0.2.2 has no accessibility tree to carry it.

Merges props onto a child element instead of rendering a native `img`. There is no DOM element graph to merge onto; a gpui `ImageSource::Custom` loader is the equivalent seam for a custom image component.
CORS setting for the image request. Browser fetch metadata with no analogue in gpui's asset system.
Native lazy loading attribute. Gpui loads a source when it is first observed; there is no viewport-distance scheduler to defer with.
Additional CSS classes.

Delay before showing the fallback, measured from mount so a slow load does not flash the initials behind it. A success inside the window renders before it elapses; a failure inside it waits for the same window rather than restarting it.
Override color from parent. Its own documented prop, not an alias: it overrides the parent `color` for everything the fallback paints, while the parent color still governs the rest.
Additional CSS classes.
